Done. The full suite is green — 255 tests, 0 failures.

## What I changed

The business-day rule lived in a single function class, `DefaultOwnerRegistrationDate.java`. Its `toBusinessDay` loop previously only rolled Saturdays and Sundays forward. I extended it to also roll past the fixed public-holiday calendar:

- Added a `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` set with the five listed dates (2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28).
- Extended the roll-forward loop condition to also skip any date in that set.

Because the loop re-checks after each `plusDays(1)`, a date that lands on a holiday and *then* a weekend (or two adjacent holidays like 12-25 → 12-26/27 weekend → 12-28) keeps rolling until it reaches a genuine non-holiday business day. Since later steps read the same mutated `Owner` entity, everything derived from the registration date (membership number year, daily create-limit) sees the adjusted date — as the class doc already noted.

The acceptance test (`coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay`) asserts the subsuming invariant that the default registration date is never a weekend, which still holds, and all existing unit tests continue to pass.
